Bladder washout solution should be sterile and isotonic (typically 0.9% sodium chloride), used at room or body temperature to avoid mucosal irritation. The note recommending chilled irrigant is not standard practice—cold fluid can cause discomfort and bladder spasm, and refrigeration risks contamination if not handled properly. Standard guidance favors room-temperature or warmed solution unless a clinician specifically orders otherwise.
